newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London firm after Dow record.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London firm after Dow record.

text.p: U.S. stocks trading in London were slightly firmer across the board in the wake of a sharp rally in New York which was triggered by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey Hawkins testimony to a U.S. congressional committee.
"Trade has been fairly quiet," said one dealer. "Prices are slightly higher," he added.

U.S. stocks roared to a new all-time high on Tuesday after Greenspan delivered what was interpreted as an upbeat report on the state of the U.S. economy, producing the Dow's fourth biggest single-day points gain in history.

"Sooner or later there will be a day of reckoning," said one trader, referring to the U.S. market's seemingly unstoppable rise. "But for the short-term everybody is saying that this market is going up."
The Dow finished 154.93 points higher at 8,061.65 on relief that Greenspan gave no hint that an increase in interest rates was imminent.
"We're looking for another 10-12 points higher at the opening today," one dealer said. "Then lets see how much more gas there is in the tank."
Waste Management, haulier and garbage handler, reported second quarter income of 41 cents a share, compared with estimates of 43 cents a share and down from 44 cents a year ago.

Elsewhere, shares in United Technologies climbed on the expectation of favourable results later today. Second-quarter earnings are forecast to rise by 16.3 percent to $1.14 per share. The stock rose $3/8 to $86-5/8.

Shares in drug firm Warner-Lambert continued to show a positive response to yesterday's results after the company nudged up its 1997 earnings per share projection by 10 cents to $3.20. The stock was up $1/2 to $143.
"Everyone is speechless. It was a knee-jerk relief reaction yesterday, no-one had even been thinking that interest rates were going up...this is turning into an orgy."
Greenspan is scheduled to continue his speech later today but traders said they were not expecting any nasty surprises.
Among share features, Boeing took centre stage. The stock climbed $1/2 to $56-3/4 after the European Commission gave preliminary approval to its planned $15 billion merger with McDonnell Douglas.
Shares in Waste Management fell $1/2 to $30-3/8 after earnings failed to match analysts' expectations.
